meta.titre: Plural Nouns: regular, irregular and compound forms
meta.sous_theme: Spelling of plurals and special cases

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In a shop in Garoua, the owner counts "five boxes, two knives, three babies' blankets" for a delivery note. Each of these plural forms follows a different rule, and mistakes with plurals are among the most common errors in school writing. The Paper 1 grammar section tests plurals with irregular nouns, compound nouns and nouns used before another noun. Learn the rules below and you will avoid most of the traps.

items: A singular noun names one thing; a plural noun names more than one.
Many plurals are made by adding *-s* (*book, books*).
A countable noun can be counted (*one pen, two pens*); an uncountable noun cannot.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Regular plurals

| Ending of the singular | Rule | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| most nouns | add -s | book, books; key, keys; boy, boys |
| -s, -x, -ch, -sh | add -es | bus, buses; box, boxes; church, churches; dish, dishes |
| consonant + y | change y to -ies | city, cities; baby, babies |
| vowel + y | add -s | day, days; key, keys |
| some nouns in -f or -fe | change to -ves | knife, knives; leaf, leaves; wife, wives; shelf, shelves |
| some nouns in -o | add -es | tomato, tomatoes; potato, potatoes; hero, heroes |

Not all nouns in -o take -es: *photo, photos*; *piano, pianos*; *radio, radios*.

### Irregular plurals

*man, men; woman, women; child, children; foot, feet; tooth, teeth; mouse, mice; person, people.* Some nouns do not change: *sheep, fish, deer, series, species*. Never add a second plural: *children* is already plural, so *childrens* is wrong.

### Uncountable nouns

*Information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment, news* and *homework* have no plural. Write *some information* or *two pieces of advice*, never *informations* or *advices*.

### Compound nouns

In a compound noun, the **main noun** takes the plural, not the last word: *sister-in-law, sisters-in-law*; *mother-in-law, mothers-in-law*; *passer-by, passers-by*; *runner-up, runners-up*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a plural noun shows ownership before another noun
variantes.contenu_markdown: If the plural ends in -s, add only an apostrophe: *the girls' football team*, *the boys' changing room*. If the plural does not end in -s, add 's: *the children's playground*, *the women's club*.

variantes.nom: Noun used before another noun with a number
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a measurement with a number and a hyphen describes a noun
variantes.contenu_markdown: The first noun stays singular: *a five-hour journey*, *a ten-year-old boy*, *a two-day meeting*. Without the hyphen, the noun is plural: *The journey took five hours.* *He is ten years old.*

sections.enonce_markdown:
Choose the correct plural to fill the gap.

Each of the \_\_\_\_\_\_ received a prize.

A) runner-ups   B) runners-up   C) runners-ups   D) runner-up

etapes.justification: *Runner-up* is made of a noun (*runner*) and an adverb (*up*).
The main noun is the person; *up* only tells us the position.

etapes.action: Put the main noun in the plural.
etapes.justification: Only the main noun changes; the other part stays the same.
*Each of the* needs a plural noun, so the singular D is wrong. Options A and C put -s at the end of a word that should not change.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The correct answer is **B) runners-up**: *Each of the runners-up received a prize.*

items.pourquoi_faux: The plural is made on the main noun, *sister*, not on *law*.
*Information* is uncountable and has no plural.
*Children* is already plural; adding -s makes a double plural.
After a consonant, the ending -y changes to -ies.
When the measure is used before a noun with hyphens, it stays singular.
items.correction_markdown: *He is a ten-year-old boy.* (or *He is ten years old.*)

items.enonce_markdown:
Write the plural of each noun.

(a) box

(b) city

(c) key

(d) knife

(e) tooth

(f) sheep

Choose the correct form.

(a) My two (brothers-in-law / brother-in-laws) live in Bamenda.

(b) Three (woman / women) were waiting at the bus stop.

(c) We need some (furniture / furnitures) for the new office.

(d) The (children's / childrens' / childrens) playground is next to the school.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **brothers-in-law.** The plural is on the main noun.

(b) **women.** It is the irregular plural, and *three* needs a plural noun.

(c) **furniture.** It is uncountable.

(d) **children's.** The plural *children* does not end in -s, so we add 's.

items.enonce_markdown:
Complete each gap with the correct form of the word in brackets.

(a) Several \_\_\_\_\_\_ stopped to help the cyclist. (passer-by)

(b) She gave me two \_\_\_\_\_\_ of good \_\_\_\_\_\_. (piece, advice)

(c) The \_\_\_\_\_\_ changing room is on the left. (boy)

(d) It was a \_\_\_\_\_\_ journey by bus. (five-hour)

(e) Both of Ntu's \_\_\_\_\_\_ are nurses. (sister-in-law)
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **passers-by.** The main noun is *passer*.

(b) **pieces ... advice.** *Advice* has no plural, so the countable word *piece* takes the plural.

(c) **boys'.** It is a plural possessive; the plural already ends in -s, so only the apostrophe is added.

(d) **five-hour.** The measure is singular before the noun.

(e) **sisters-in-law.** The main noun takes the plural.

items_markdown: Add -es after -s, -x, -ch, -sh; change consonant + y to -ies; add -s after vowel + y.
Learn the irregular plurals (*men, women, children, feet, teeth, mice, people*) and the words that do not change (*sheep, fish*).
Uncountable nouns (*information, advice, furniture, luggage*) have no plural: use *a piece of* or *some*.
In a compound noun the main noun takes the plural: *sisters-in-law*, *passers-by*, *runners-up*.
Plural possessive: *girls'* (after -s) and *children's* (no -s); a measure before a noun stays singular (*a five-hour journey*).
